newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude ends lower on ample supply, technicals.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude ends lower on ample supply, technicals.

text.p: NYMEX crude ended lower for the third consecutive session Thursday as increasing domestic supply and the prospect of $2 billion worth of Iraqi oil for another six months continued to weigh on the market.
"There is a general sense that storage levels are rising and that crude does not deserve a premium given the supply situation," said Mike De Luca, trader with Prudential Securities.
July crude settled off 46 cents at $19.66 a barrel.
Technical selling sharpened losses in the morning after sell stops were triggered when the spot month fell beneath the psychological support level of $20.00, chartists said.
Prompt crude was technically weakened going into Thursday's session after breaking key trendline support on Wednesday that extended from the $18.96 double bottom made April 10 on the spot chart.
Chartists noted a shelf of support on the spot chart between 19.40 and 19.50 set in early May that could underpin the prompt month early on Friday.
Refined products followed crude for the most part with July heating oil finishing down 0.84 cent at 53.32 cents a gallon and July reformulated gasoline ending 0.60 cent lower at 59.82 cents a gallon.
Gasoline, however, could face further weakness as the New York Harbor spot market was absorbing a steady stream of supply, dealers said. NYMEX gasoline is deliverable in the Harbor.
The Harbor is sated by healthy imports and heavy shipments from the Colonial Pipeline.

Adding to supply was a delivery into the Harbor by midcontinent refiner Koch Industries to oil major British Petroleum against the June contract. BP said it was taking between one million and 1.5 million barrels of gasoline.

"Some thought that we were going to see a relatively tight market in June, but then people heard of the large delivery and high production," said Todd Miller, a dealer with Morgan Stanley in New York.

On Tuesday, the American Petroleum Institute (API) said that for the week ended May 30 U.S. refiner gasoline output stood at 8.195 million barrels a day, a record high. The same data showed domestic crude stocks swelling by 8.4 million barrels.

Fundamentals for crude weakened further on Wednesday when the United Nations Security Council formally approved the renewal of the Iraqi oil-for-food accord on Wednesday, as expected. Under the deal, Iraq is allowed to sell $2 billion worth of crude for six months in exchange for humanitarian aid.

With supply contracts expected to be rolled over from the first six months, Iraq's ambassador to the United Nations Nizar Hamdoon said Iraqi oil liftings should occur without a delay upon the deal's extension that starts June 8.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
